entities.name: PMID:10750630
observations: Direct comparison of 35 patients with painful postherpetic neuralgia and 34 patients with peripheral vestibular vertigo using SCL-90-R and psychiatrist-administered Diagnostic Interview Schedule.

PHN patients had significantly more major-depression and somatization symptoms, but no significant difference in formal psychiatric diagnoses; vestibular patients had more acutely distressing somatic symptoms.

entities.name: Postherpetic neuralgia
observations: In the direct comparison, PHN was associated with greater depressive and somatization symptom burden than peripheral vestibular disease, without a significant difference in formal psychiatric diagnoses.

entities.name: Peripheral vestibular disease
observations: In the direct comparison, patients had more acutely distressing somatic symptoms than PHN patients, despite fewer depressive and somatization symptoms.

entities.name: PHN versus vestibular symptoms
observations: A small direct study found that psychiatric symptom profiles differed: PHN had more depressive and somatization symptoms, while peripheral vestibular disease had more acute somatic distress; formal psychiatric diagnoses did not differ significantly.
The accessible abstract did not report means, effect sizes, confidence intervals, or exact p values.
